channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Dems take back Congress, Maine GOP Sen. Collins concedes
item.description: Collins is the five-term senator from Maine.

item.title: Troy Jackson wins Maine Senate race over Susan Collins, in major coup for Democrats
item.description: The result is a crucial victory for Democrats in their push to retake the Senate majority, flipping a seat that Collins has held for nearly 30 years. (Image credit: Ashley L. Conti for NPR)

item.title: These candidates made history in the 2026 midterm elections
item.description: The midterms saw an expansion of representation among America's lawmakers, with several candidates celebrating groundbreaking wins.

item.title: Here's how some key demographic groups voted in the midterms
item.description: These charts show how various demographic groups voted in the midterm election. The data comes from a poll of tens of thousands of voters, conducted by the firm SSRS for a number of news outlets. (Image credit: Tommy Martino)

item.title: Democrats projected to take Congress in blue wave fueled by Trump, economy discontent
item.description: Democrats will win enough seats in the U.S. House of Representatives to gain control of the lower chamber of Congress from Republicans, ABC projects.

item.title: South Africans vote in local elections that could continue decline of ANC
item.description: South Africans have begun voting in local elections that are seen as an evaluation of the party that led the country out of white minority rule

item.title: Midterms: Why is California slower at counting its votes?
item.description: California polls have just closed, but results will take longer to come in. Why does the state take longer to count its votes? We discuss this with our guest, Guy Marzorati, political correspondent at KQED in the Bay Area.

item.title: US midterms: "Keeping our fingers crossed" (Leila Meresman)
item.description: Democrats who once saw the political map as an almost impossible lift are now hopeful that a Senate majority is within reach, even though their path runs through several more conservative states. We discuss this with our guest Leila Meresman, spokesperson of Democrats Abroad France says.

item.title: Former Arkansas governor says Democrats' gains are 'more significant than ever anticipated'
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with former Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson about Democratic victories in states typically considered Republican strongholds. (Image credit: Danny Johnston)

item.title: US midterms: Democrats celebrate early victories at a watch party in Los Angeles
item.description: Our correspondent Wassim Cornet reports from a Democratic watch party in Los Angeles where "people are opening bottles of champagne" following the Democrats' first victories in these midterm elections. We also speak with France 24's Jessica Le Masurier, reporting from Detroit, Michigan.

WATCH: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott addresses supporters after conceding governor's race
item.description: Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott addressed supporters after ABC News projected Democrat Gina Hinojosa will win the state's race for governor.

item.title: WATCH: Amy Acton addresses supporters after projected win in Ohio governor's race
item.description: Democrat Amy Acton addressed supporters after ABC News projected she will win the Ohio governor's race over Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.

item.title: Democrats win full control of Congress, ushering in a new era of divided government
item.description: The victories in the House and Senate return Democrats to full control of Congress for the first time since 2023 and deepens the level of expected friction between them and President Trump. (Image credit: Cliff Owen)

item.title: WATCH: Vivek Ramaswamy addresses supporters after projected defeat in Ohio governor's race
item.description: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy addressed supporters after ABC News projected Democrat Amy Acton will win the Ohio governor's race.

item.title: WATCH: Annie Andrews addresses supporters after projected win in South Carolina Senate race
item.description: Democrat Annie Andrews addressed supporters after ABC News projected her the winner of the South Carolina Senate race, flipping the seat once held by the late Lindsey Graham.

item.title: Democrat Josh Turek wins the Senate seat in Iowa
item.description: Democrat Josh Turek has defeated Sen. Ashley Hinson in Iowa, according to a race call by the Associated Press. (Image credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

item.title: On a historic night for democratic socialists, Mamdani says midterms show power of working-class voters
item.description: The New York mayor tells NPR's Juana Summers that newly elected democratic socialists need to seize this moment and show voters what politics can deliver. (Image credit: Adam Gray)

item.title: WATCH: Keisha Lance Bottoms addresses supporters after projected win in Georgia gov. race
item.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms addressed supporters after ABC News projected her the winner of the Georgia governor's race, making her the first Black female governor in the history of the U.S.

item.title: Democrat David Crowley will be Wisconsin's first Black governor
item.description: Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Congressman Tom Tiffany in a campaign that focused on "lowering costs for working families" and bringing more jobs to Wisconsin. (Image credit: Nam Y. Huh)

item.title: Adam Hamilton becomes the first Democratic senator from Kansas in nearly a century
item.description: Democrat Adam Hamilton beat Sen. Roger Marshall, a fierce loyalist to President Trump, per a race call by the Associated Press. (Image credit: Jim Vondruska/Getty Images)

item.title: Missourians reject ballot proposal that would have re-imposed an abortion ban
item.description: Missouri voters defeated a measure that would have banned abortion just two years after voters legalized abortion in another vote. Voters in Missouri legalized abortion two years ago but this time the abortion ban was coupled with a ban on transgender treatment for minors. Opponents said it was misleading. (Image credit: Jason Rosenbaum)

item.title: WATCH: House Speaker Mike Johnson speaks after Democrats projected to take control of House
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson made remarks after ABC News projected Democrats will win enough seats to take control of the House.

item.title: Democrat Gina Hinojosa wins race for Texas governor, ousting Greg Abbott
item.description: Hinojosa, an Austin state representative, is set to be the state's first Democratic governor since 1995 and will be the state's first Latina governor. (Image credit: Michael Gonzalez)

item.title: Key US Senate results: Democrats win upper chamber with victories in Texas and Iowa
item.description: Democrats won control of the Senate in the US midterm elections Tuesday, with initial results showing the party securing shock victories in Texas, Ohio, North and South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.

item.title: US midterms: "Voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump"
item.description: The polls in these midterm elections suggest that "this will either be a good night or a historic night for Democrats". But what is driving this momentum? We discuss this with our guest, Mallory Newall, Senior Vice President at Ipsos. "We've seen in our polling at Ipsos in recent weeks and months that voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump," she says.

item.title: US: "Even in places where the Democrats haven't won, the swing towards them has been significant"
item.description: Tens of millions of Americans cast their vote in the crucial polls that have been pitched as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency amid anger at surging petrol prices, tariffs and the Iran war. We discuss the first results with France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani and Fraser Jackson. "Even in places where the Democrats haven't won, the swing towards them has been significant", he says.

item.title: Democratic gains mount in US midterms as Trump faces bruising verdict
item.description: Democrats notched a string of early victories in US midterm elections Tuesday, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat and making inroads in conservative House districts as President Donald Trump faced the prospect of a bruising election setback. France 24's Douglas Herbert gives us his analysis.

item.title: REPLAY: Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff wins reelection
item.description: Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff was reelected Tuesday to a second term, holding a key seat for Democrats by defeating Republican Representative Mike Collins in a race that catapulted the Senate’s youngest member to the forefront of his party’s national stars as it looks to stymie President Donald Trump in his final years in the White House.

item.title: Ukrainian GCSE to be offered to British students
item.description: Students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be able to take a Ukrainian GCSE from 2028 as part of government plans.

item.title: WATCH: Jon Ossoff addresses supporters after projected win in Georgia Senate race
item.description: Democrat Jon Ossoff addressed supporters after ABC News projected he will win reelection in the Georgia Senate race.

item.title: Midterms: Abdul El-Sayed, Mike Rogers face off for Michigan Senate seat
item.description: With New Hampshire and Georgia staying in Democratic hands, Republicans now look to Michigan for a pickup, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is competing with Republican Mike Rogers. France 24's Jessica Le Masurier reports from a Democratic watch party in Detroit.

item.title: US midterm elections: Democrats flip Senate seat in North Carolina
item.description: Democrats have flipped a Senate seat in North Carolina as they try to recapture majorities in Congress and break Republicans’ unified hold on power in Washington. France 24's Florence Villeminot walks us through the US electoral map.

item.title: Parliament risks 'catastrophic event' without urgent renovation
item.description: The Palace of Westminster is at risk of a "catastrophic event" if delays to a renovation initiative are not resolved, a group of MPs have warned.

item.title: TAKEOVER - LINK - 2024 ELEX MAP
WATCH: Election Day draws millions of Americans to the polls
item.description: Americans from Michigan to Maine, Texas to Kansas lined up to make their voices heard on Pres. Trump’s policies and which party will control Congress.

item.title: US democracy, Trump fatigue, cost of living are top issues with voters, AP survey finds
item.description: Roughly 6 in 10 voters deeply disapprove of US President Donald Trump's presidency, according to an AP survey released Tuesday. About 4 in 10 say the economy is the most important issue while 3 in 10 say the state of US democracy is of primary concern – well above the number that rated crime or immigration as most important.

item.title: DOJ ramps up probe of Alaska Senate race with target letters, new subpoenas: Sources
item.description: The DOJ has continued moving at an aggressive clip in ramping up its criminal investigation into the Alaska U.S. Senate race, sources tell ABC News.

item.title: Historian Timothy Snyder: Trump running US foreign policy 'as though he were an organized criminal'
item.description: As Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections, François Picard welcomes historian Timothy Snyder, professor at the University of Toronto's Munk School of Global Affairs, for a conversation about the future of American democracy, the growing political influence of technology billionaires and the dangers of a new Gilded Age. Who really holds power in Donald Trump's America: the president or the billionaires surrounding him?

item.title: Trump tariffs hitting small businesses
item.description: As US voters cast their ballots in the midterm elections, the economy remained their top concern. Despite robust headline macroeconomic data, middle-class Americans are growing increasingly frustrated with the rising cost of living. Meanwhile, Donald Trump's tariffs have hit small businesses hard, leading to a significant rise in bankruptcies. Our correspondents met with some business owners.

item.title: South Africa braces for some job losses as AGOA ends
item.description: In tonight's edition, Rwanda and South Africa will lose their duty-free access to the U.S. market after being excluded from the AGOA trade program. Also, South Africans head to the polls amid water shortages and frustration with local services. And in the DRC's mining capital, Kolwezi, residents are taking on one of the country's largest Chinese-owned mines... accusing it of poisoning their environment.

item.title: Trump promised a 'Golden Age'. What has he delivered at home?
item.description: Donald Trump promised Americans a “Golden Age” when he returned to the White House in January 2025. Since then, his administration has slashed government spending through DOGE, ramped up mass deportations, expanded ICE operations and pursued an aggressive crackdown on DEI programmes and transgender rights. But how much has he actually achieved, and at what cost? Vedika Bahl examines Trump's domestic agenda since returning to office.

item.title: Spain's transport minister to resign after train crash killed 69 people
item.description: Spain's transport minister has said he will step down after two deadly train crashes in less than a year.

item.title: WATCH: Latino voters emerge as critical voting bloc in midterms
item.description: Héctor Sánchez Barba, president and CEO of Mi Familia Vota, discusses the diverse electorate emerging as a swing group in some key races.

item.title: Trickle or tsunami? Democrats eye gains in US midterm elections
item.description: Will it be a trickle, a wave, or a tsunami? Election Day in the United States with Democrats hoping to take back one or both houses of Congress. We’ll track the turnout, gauge the mood and raise the curtain ahead of Midterms results that are sure to shape the last two years of Donald Trump’s second and final term. Will a US president who’s already broken norms with his maximum use of executive powers be affected by the results a little, a lot, or not at all?

item.title: Where do gas prices stand in key states on Election Day?
item.description: Fuel prices vary across the states expected to determine control of the Senate.

item.title: Third teen arrested on suspicion of attempted murder over stabbing at Halloween party
item.description: A third boy has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after five teenagers were seriously injured when they were allegedly stabbed at a party on Halloween.

item.title: France's dermatology crisis: Patients desperate for appointments
item.description: Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year. Yet as more and more patients seek medical advice, getting an appointment with a dermatologist is becoming increasingly difficult. Half the country's dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only around 100 new specialists are trained up each year. Faced with this growing shortage, some are coming up with innovative solutions. FRANCE 24's Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello report.

item.title: Family wealth, Epstein, ‘vanity projects’: How Democrats plan to investigate Trump after midterms
item.description: Democrats are preparing to launch a flurry of investigations into President Donald Trump’s administration and business dealings if they retake one or both chambers of Congress, devising strategies to circumvent obstruction from the White House and avoid the impeachment deadlock that consumed the US legislature during Trump’s first term in office.

item.title: Russian households face increasing financial strain as war in Ukraine drags on
item.description: As Moscow continues to launch strikes across Ukraine, Russian citizens are facing increasing financial strain. Since the start of the war in 2022, utility bills in Russia have risen by more than 50% – over 13% this year alone. These rising costs come as the country grapples with ongoing drone attacks originating from Ukraine.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia are taking the war underground as drones saturate the battlefield
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last week heralded the success of Operation Veles, during which Kyiv sent troops deep into a disused gas pipeline in the Kupiansk region to confront Russian troops. These underground tactics, which Russian forces have been using for more than two years to slip past Ukrainian lines, are giving Kyiv a new strategy on the battlefield.

item.title: MPs urge online retailers to stop selling AI toys over child harm fears
item.description: AI toys with built-in chatbots could expose children to psychological harms and inappropriate material, according to MPs and peers who are urging Amazon and eBay to stop selling them.

item.title: Andrew compelled to testify at businessman's fraud trial
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been served a summons compelling him to give evidence at a Turkish businessman's fraud trial, Sky News understands.

item.title: Reform councillor charged with 35 offences including 12 counts of rape
item.description: A Reform UK councillor says he is "shocked and dismayed" after being charged with 35 offences, including 12 counts of rape.

item.title: WATCH: New states in play as record gas prices hit on Election Day
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Washington Correspondent Jon Karl and Chief Business Correspondent Rebecca Jarvis break down why states in deep-red territory are in play and the state of the economy on Election Day.

item.title: Australia's social media ban challenged by Reddit and rights group in court
item.description: Australia's landmark social media ban for under-16s faces challenges in court over accusations that it amounts to censorship and creates privacy issues.

item.title: Bomb threats reported on multiple flights, including two from UK airports
item.description: At least seven flights, including two from the UK, have been affected by bomb threats, which caused unplanned landings and temporary airport closures.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares New Jersey students' determination in 100-Yard Food Drive Challenge
item.description: Students at Howell High School filled their football field with over a quarter million pounds of food for the nonprofit, Dermer Dreams. David Muir reports on the volunteers that delivered.

item.title: WATCH: Lucky fisherman catches fish worth $1M
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mechanic in Australia whose life just changed by a fishing contest.

item.title: WATCH: Man complete 31,000-mile walk around the world after 28 years
item.description: A British adventurer who has been walking around the world for almost three decades returned to his childhood home Monday.

item.title: Spanish footballer dies after on-field collision
item.description: Tenerife football player Jesus de Miguel has died after suffering a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision in a match on Monday.

item.title: WATCH: 5 people at Chili's in North Carolina suffer burns after margarita mix-up
item.description: Three customers and two employees at a Chili's restaurant suffered chemical burns after an employee mistakenly used a cleaning powder instead of sugar to make the drinks, health officials say.

item.title: Cyber attacks affect UK meat processing industry, top security official says
item.description: Cyber attacks have affected the UK meat processing industry, a top security official has said in the wake of hacks that hit supermarkets across Europe.

item.title: US carries out 'limited strikes' on Qeshm Island in Iran
item.description: The US military has carried out "limited strikes" on Qeshm Island in Iran - hours before the midterms are due to take place.

item.title: British troops will be allowed to fire at Russian forces if attacked during multinational mission
item.description: British troops will be allowed to fire back at Russian forces if attacked as part of a multinational mission to secure any future peace in Ukraine, Western officials have said.

item.title: WATCH: Video of ICE agent apparently pointing gun in bystander's face during arrest
item.description: ICE is facing new scrutiny over a video that allegedly shows an ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a bystander in California.

item.title: 'Everything is destroyed': Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.
